correctness.rationale: A fresh outer-cycle/spokes/pentagram representation yielded six perfect matchings, each with a complement of two 5-cycles, so three colors cannot work. Dynamic most-constrained-first enumeration constructed exactly 49920 proper assignments with four named colors. Bucketing pairs of proper assignments by their common 14-coordinate signature recovers exactly single-edge steps; an independent flood-fill gave 960 singleton components and two components of order 24480 with 54720 edges apiece (109440 total). Transport to KG(5,2) and evaluation of all named-palette permutations and ground-symbol permutations reproduced both phase actions, the full transitive S5×S4 action on the frozen states, and their edge-class sizes 3,4,4,4. At a cubic edge there are four other incident edges, not three: the prose criterion should mean their colors collectively take all three alternative values. The actual set-size predicate |F_e(c)|=3 is correct and the Finding is unaffected. Replay: python3 /workspace/branches/independent_petersen.py, output independent_petersen.out alongside. No Kempe-chain or other simultaneous changes are counted.

evidence: A palette permutation multiplies each of ten vertex signs by the same palette sign, hence fixes the product. For a symbol permutation the multiplier on the product is the product of the signs of the induced local incident-edge reorderings, independent of the state. It is a character S5→{±1}. The reported transposition swaps the two mobile sign classes, so the character is the usual sign.

Thus the two reported frozen A5×S4 orbits lie one in each nonempty sign class, and an odd symbol permutation fuses them into a single S5×S4 orbit. This is not a contradiction with the subgroup orbit count.

A color missing at k vertices occurs on (10−k)/2 edges. The published missing multiplicity 4,2,2,2 implies sizes 3,4,4,4. An odd symbol permutation switches the two mobile components, so their identical edge counts each equal 109440/2.
